data_analytics.scenario: Bangladesh Bank publishes monthly data on Mobile Financial Services (MFS) platforms such as bKash, Nagad and Rocket. You're asked to look at one year of change and explain what it means.
data_pack: Monthly transaction volume: Tk 1.30 trillion (Jan 2024) -> Tk 1.72 trillion (Jan 2025), +32.56%

questions.question: Accounts grew about 9% while transaction value grew about 33%. What does this gap most likely mean?
options: The data must contain an error
Existing users are transacting more, not just new users joining
MFS usage is actually declining
Transaction value and account count should always move together
questions.correct_answer: Existing users are transacting more, not just new users joining
questions.explanation: When a value metric grows much faster than a count metric, the most likely driver is existing accounts being used more heavily, not only new signups.

data_analytics.source_name: Bangladesh Bank data, reported by The Financial Express

business_analysis.scenario: Bangladesh's Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) tracks export earnings by product category. You're asked, as a business analyst, to assess a concentration risk.
data_pack: Ready-made garment (RMG) exports: US$19.89 billion (about 81% of total exports)

questions.question: One product category (RMG) makes up about 81% of total exports. From a risk-management view, what does this concentration create?
options: No risk, since RMG is currently growing
A dependency risk - any shock to RMG demand would affect the whole economy's exports
Proof that other export categories should be shut down
A sign that the underlying data is unreliable
questions.correct_answer: A dependency risk - any shock to RMG demand would affect the whole economy's exports
questions.explanation: Heavy concentration in one category means the whole export base is exposed to whatever affects that one category (e.g. demand shocks, tariffs, competition).

business_analysis.source_name: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data, reported by Apparel Resources

marketing.scenario: The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) publishes subscriber counts that marketers use to size the online audience.
data_pack: Mobile internet users made up 118.49 million of the 131 million total in 2023

questions.question: The online audience more than doubled in 8 years and is overwhelmingly mobile. What should this tell you as you plan a digital campaign?
options: A broadband-only campaign will reach nearly everyone
A mobile-first creative and format strategy will reach the largest share of the audience
Audience size doesn't matter for campaign planning
Growth this fast usually reverses within a year
questions.correct_answer: A mobile-first creative and format strategy will reach the largest share of the audience
questions.explanation: With the large majority of internet users on mobile, formats and creative that work well on small screens and mobile data reach the biggest share of the audience.

marketing.source_name: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC), reported by The Financial Express

finance.scenario: Bangladesh Bank tracks monthly remittances sent home by expatriate workers, an important source of foreign currency.
data_pack: FY2024-25 total remittances: US$30.32 billion (+26.8% year-on-year, a record)

questions.question: Remittances jumped about 27% in a single year to a record high. Before using this as a stable trend in a forecast, what should a finance analyst check first?
options: Nothing - a record high is always a stable base for forecasting
Whether the jump is driven by one-off factors, or reflects a genuine, sustained shift
Only the percentage change, and ignore the underlying dollar figures
Whether the number was reported by a newspaper
questions.correct_answer: Whether the jump is driven by one-off factors, or reflects a genuine, sustained shift
questions.explanation: A single record year can be driven by temporary factors (policy changes, exchange-rate incentives, seasonal effects); a forecast needs to separate those from a durable trend.

finance.source_name: Bangladesh Bank data, reported by UNB

hr.scenario: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) runs an annual Labour Force Survey covering employment across the country.
data_pack: Unemployment rate among bachelor's-degree holders: 13.5% (2024), up from 13.1% (2023)

questions.question: Graduate unemployment (13.5%) is nearly 4x the national rate (3.66%). What should HR investigate before concluding graduates are simply 'unemployable'?
options: Nothing further - the gap speaks for itself
Whether there's a mismatch between the skills graduates have and what local employers actually need
Whether to stop hiring graduates altogether
Whether the national rate itself is wrong
questions.correct_answer: Whether there's a mismatch between the skills graduates have and what local employers actually need
questions.explanation: A large gap between graduate and overall unemployment usually points to a skills/expectations mismatch, not a lack of effort or ability.

hr.source_name: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), Labour Force Survey 2024, reported by The Financial Express

technology.case_title: A subscriber base that fell, then recovered
technology.scenario: BTRC publishes monthly counts of active mobile and internet subscribers, a rough proxy for a tech product's active-user base.
data_pack: Internet subscribers fell for 8 straight months before March 2025
March 2025: rebounded with about 750,000 new users, after only about 10,000 added in February

questions.question: A user base fell for 8 straight months, then suddenly jumped by about 750,000 in one month. Before reporting 'we fixed churn', what should you check?
options: Nothing - any jump is automatically good news
Whether the jump reflects genuine reactivation/new demand, or a one-off event (promotion, reporting change, seasonal effect)
Only whether the dashboard is displaying the number correctly
Whether competitors saw the same jump, and stop there
questions.correct_answer: Whether the jump reflects genuine reactivation/new demand, or a one-off event (promotion, reporting change, seasonal effect)
questions.explanation: A sudden reversal after a long decline needs a specific cause identified before it's safe to claim the underlying problem is fixed.

technology.source_name: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) data, reported by MeaTechWatch and Prothom Alo

supply_chain.case_title: Knitwear vs. woven garment export growth
supply_chain.scenario: The Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) breaks down Bangladesh's largest export sector, ready-made garments, into its two main product lines.
data_pack: Woven garment exports (FY2024-25): US$18.19 billion (+7.82% year-on-year)

questions.question: Knitwear grew faster (+9.73%) than woven garments (+7.82%) this year. What should an operations coordinator check before shifting resources toward knitwear?
options: Nothing - faster growth always means shift all resources immediately
Whether the growth is sustained (not a one-off order spike) and whether current supplier/capacity can support a shift
Whether woven garments should be discontinued entirely
Only the export dollar totals, and ignore the growth rates
questions.correct_answer: Whether the growth is sustained (not a one-off order spike) and whether current supplier/capacity can support a shift
questions.explanation: One year of faster growth in one segment isn't enough on its own to justify a capacity shift - it needs to be checked against trend durability and actual supplier/capacity readiness.

supply_chain.source_name: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data, reported by Apparel Resources

general.scenario: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) runs a Quarterly Labour Force Survey covering the whole working-age population.
data_pack: Labour force (working or looking for work): 73.75 million

questions.question: Of about 173 million people surveyed, only about 74 million are in the labour force. What should you ask to understand who the other ~99 million are?
options: Nothing - they must all be unemployed
Their age, education status, and caregiving/study roles, since 'not in the labour force' isn't the same as 'unemployed'
Whether the survey itself was conducted correctly, and stop there
Whether the number is a typo
questions.correct_answer: Their age, education status, and caregiving/study roles, since 'not in the labour force' isn't the same as 'unemployed'
questions.explanation: The labour force excludes children, students, retirees, and people not seeking work for other reasons - none of whom are 'unemployed' in the usual sense.

general.source_name: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), Quarterly Labour Force Survey, reported by Dhaka Tribune
